newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian tin, nickel rally, other base metals steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian tin, nickel rally, other base metals steady.

text.p: Indian tin and nickel prices bounced back on Tuesday but other base metals were steady, dealers said.
Sentiment was firm on increased physical enquiries, Sharad Parikh, president of the Bombay Metal Exchange, said.
Tin prices rose 200 rupees to 30,400 rupees per quintal after losing 700 rupees last week while nickel rose 200 rupees to 35,600 rupees per quintal after losing 800 rupees last week.
"Fresh physical buying as well as a rally in the world market helped local prices bounce back," Parikh said.
Copper was steady at 13,875 rupees per quintal after losing 50 rupees on Monday while zinc was quiet at 8,100 rupees, dealers said.
Lead and aluminium were unchanged at 4,100 rupees and 7,700 rupees per quintal respectively, they said.
Overall market sentiment was firm at close of the session on increased physical enquiries and reports of an uptrend in the world market.
